title: LCLI-792 follow-ups from the round-3 verdict: contended-path rehash, sync-plan test gaps, raw-byte digest
description:
Follow-up from the #746 round-3 APPROVE (verdict recorded verbatim on LCLI-792). Done inside lore's slack; GATES the 0.15.1 bump (LBUMP). Own PR, own reviewer.
- S1 (correctness): set waited = true on every EEXIST/exists outcome BEFORE the snapshot === null branch at src/core/advisory-lock.ts (~:699-710), so a caller whose follow-up read finds the lock gone still rehashes once it owns it. Without it a check computed against a tree a departing sync just rewrote is keyed by the pre-sync hash and a waiter with that pre-sync tree can replay it. A test must go red without the change.
- S2: (a) a beforeDigest: null case: the holder planned a file as absent and the waiter's checkout gains that file during the wait; it must abandon. (b) assert applySyncWritePlan returns true at test/lcli792-advisory-command.test.ts (~:326). (c) assert the lock OWNER, not just existence, inside adopt at test/advisory-lock.test.ts (~:1369).
- N1: hash raw bytes, not decoded text (sync.ts digestOf; the reads decode utf8, so distinct invalid sequences collapse to U+FFFD).
- N2: one doc sentence on applySyncWritePlan: derived plan files (index.md, log.md) can be written stale if a concept is retitled during the wait; the next sync corrects it.
- N3: a throw inside adopt (assertNoSymlinkInAnyPath, non-ENOENT read error) abandons and recomputes, or say why it propagates.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test red without the S1 change shows a caller that finds the lock vanished after EEXIST rehashes once it owns the lock
The three S2 test gaps are closed, each assertion able to go red
The plan digest hashes raw bytes (N1) and the applySyncWritePlan doc names the derived-file residual (N2)
An adopt throw either abandons and recomputes or the doc says why it propagates (N3)

implementationNotes:
REQUEST CHANGES at b88fc820 (opum-ai/lore-cli#758, LCLI-810). The fixes themselves are sound. One blocker: S2b is not done at the line round 3 cited. Change that line and this becomes APPROVE.

I ran no shell, no tests and no mutants. Everything below comes from reading files at head.

BLOCKER
B1. S2b. `test/lcli792-advisory-command.test.ts:326` is still a bare `await applySyncWritePlan(other, plans[0] as SyncWritePlan);` that throws away the return value.
- The only reuse-path assertion of `true` is `appliedOk` at :397/:410.
- The new S2a block starts at :516, below :326, so it did not shift that line. :326 is most likely the exact line round 3 cited.
- I cannot tell whether :410 is new in this commit. Ask the writer for `git show b88fc820 -- test/lcli792-advisory-command.test.ts`. If :410 is new and round 3 meant that test, downgrade this to a nit.
- What already covers it: the byte comparison at :327-331 goes red on a refusal, because `applySyncWritePlan` writes nothing before returning false (sync.ts:470-477). It does not catch a "writes, then returns false" mutant, which is what the assert exists for.
- Fix, one line: `expect(await applySyncWritePlan(other, plans[0] as SyncWritePlan)).toBe(true);`

SHOULD-FIX (older than this PR; route it, don't hold the PR on it)
SF1. One path to S1's harm remains, without any EEXIST.
- `advisory-run.ts:155` computes the entry hash with several git spawns BEFORE `withAdvisoryResult` begins. The first `tryCreateLock` is at `advisory-lock.ts:654`.
- Sequence: a sync holder in the same worktree writes and releases after that hash but before the first create attempt. The check then acquires on its first try with `waited === false`. :674-677 keys its result by the stale entry hash, and it computes against the post-sync tree.
- A waiter in another worktree still on the pre-sync tree can then replay it (finishedAt > startedAt holds). That is exactly S1's consequence.
- The comment at :672-673 (round-2 nit 6) assumes this cannot happen. That conflicts with putting the hash before the lock.
- Options: always call `rehash` once the lock is held when one is supplied (undoing nit 6), or take the entry hash inside the call after `startedAt` and treat any result whose finishedAt falls after the hash time as a wait.
- S1 within its literal scope IS closed:
  - `waited = true` at :702 runs before both `continue`s (:709 snapshot-null, :722 "broke").
  - Every `unlock` return writes no result slot (:767-777), and created/error returns before contending (:663-668).
  - No other early return skips it.
  - The S1 test (:1397-1423) would go red if :702 moved below :710: there would be no rehash, so `rehashes` would be 0 against 1 at :1420, and the slot would hold "entry" against "after-the-holder" at :1422. The fake sleep removes the lock, so the second pass acquires.

NITS
N-a. S2c is weaker than the writer's account says.
- `expect(lock.pid).toBe(process.pid)` at :1378 can never fail: holder and waiter run in the same process.
- Only `owner !== holderOwner` at :1379 discriminates.
- Since N3, an `expect` that throws inside `adopt` is caught by `adoptOrAbandon` (advisory-lock.ts:749-755) and becomes `false`. Those in-callback asserts therefore cannot fail the test directly. In the `accept=false` iteration they are inert.
- A release-before-adopt or adopt-without-lock mutant still goes red, but only through the `accept=true` iteration's outer checks (:1391-1393, reused/computes).
- Suggest recording the owner into an outer variable and asserting after the call.
N-b. The S1 test skips with a silent `return` on win32 and on root (:1398). It passes without testing anything on the windows-latest required leg. Use `test.skipIf` so the skip is visible.
N-c. `applySyncWritePlan` reads each file twice: raw at sync.ts:473, decoded for rollback at :476. Rollback therefore restores decoded text, so a file with invalid UTF-8 comes back as U+FFFD. `runSync`'s own `before` has the same pattern; this is cosmetic.
N-d. If `sweepTrackerStorage` throws at sync.ts:486, the docs writes have already landed. The abandon then recomputes on that tree, still keyed by the keyHash taken before adopt (advisory-lock.ts:674). This fails safe: any later reuse is re-gated by the pre-image check. It also matches what an uncontended `runSync` leaves when its sweep fails at :390. Not a defect, but the docstring at :449-450 should not imply nothing was written.

CHECKS THAT HOLD
3/N1. Both sides use raw bytes.
- Holder: `beforeDigest: digestOf(rawBytesIfPresent(...))` at sync.ts:377. This is the only producer of a plan. `readSource`'s decoded `before` (:300, :313) is never digested.
- Waiter: raw at :473, compared as raw bytes against `Buffer.from(after)` at :474, digest at :475.
- The declared gap (a holder that digests decoded text is not mutation-covered) is low risk. The current code is raw on the one path. A decoded-text holder would mismatch any raw waiter for invalid UTF-8, which abandons. It could falsely match only when the waiter's file holds exactly encode(decode(holder_raw)).
- The two-invalid-files test (:533-549) catches a waiter-side decode mutant through its control at :547.
- CRLF still only abandons: CRLF bytes ≠ LF `after` (:474), then the digest mismatch returns false (:475) before anything is written.
2/S2a is real (:519-531). A "null means always write" mutant goes red at :529. Swapping the equality and digest checks goes red at :526. It tests the apply directly rather than an end-to-end abandon, which is enough.
4/N3. A throw before :483 writes nothing (the symlink preflight is at :460, every pre-image check runs before :478). `writeManyAtomicOrRollback` rolls back its own throw. The recompute (`options.compute()` at advisory-lock.ts:688) sits outside `adoptOrAbandon`, so real errors still propagate, and the finally block at :693-696 releases the lock. The N3 test (:1425-1463) goes red if the try/catch is removed: the waiter would reject.
5. (a14) Q1: the apply runs under the lock (:679-685). Its order matches the ruling: skip if equal to `after`, write only if equal to the pre-image, otherwise abandon (sync.ts:474-475). (a16): `isLockSnapshotStale` at :901-924 still returns false for a same-host live pid whatever its age. Q3: abandoning or adopting writes nothing to stderr or stdout. Only `unlock` emits a line, once (`onceNotices`, :758-765).
N2. The derived-files paragraph is in the JSDoc at sync.ts:444-447. My grep under docs/ only covered filenames matching *advisory*, so I cannot say whether a lore docs page also changed.

COULD NOT CONFIRM WITHOUT A SHELL
- The commit's changed-file set, so DEC-182 (1) is unverified. The changes I saw are in src/core/advisory-lock.ts, src/commands/sync.ts, test/advisory-lock.test.ts and test/lcli792-advisory-command.test.ts, none in a DEC-182 path class. Ask for `git show --stat b88fc820` to confirm that nothing in .github/, package.json, bun.lock, hooks or scripts/ moved.
- Any test or mutant result, including whether bun:test fails a test when an `expect` throws inside a callback and is then caught (this matters for N-a).
- Tracker: no file at this head mentions LCLI-810. No `.quest` record exists, and a search of the whole tree is empty. The task record may be missing, or may live only on another branch.

REQUEST CHANGES at a42a863d (opum-ai/lore-cli#758, LCLI-810, round 2). All five rulings are carried out correctly. One blocker remains, on the abandon-then-compute path you asked me to check: the result key there is post-lock but taken BEFORE adopt, and adopt itself can write. That reintroduces SF1's harm, and it falsifies the "fails safe" sentence N-d added. I ran no shell, no tests and no mutants. Everything below comes from reading files at this head.

BLOCKER
B2. A result keyed by a tree it was not computed against, through adopt's own writes.
- advisory-lock.ts:678 computes keyHash (the post-lock rehash) before the adopt attempt at :685.
- The sync adopt is applySyncWritePlan. It writes at sync.ts:486, then runs sweepTrackerStorage at :489, which can throw. It throws only on a Backlog bundle; the Quest sweep is a no-op (:455-457, :394-395).
- adoptOrAbandon (advisory-lock.ts:749-755) turns that throw into false. compute() at :688 then runs on the POST-write tree, and :690 stores its result under the PRE-adopt keyHash.
- runSync records only files that actually change (sync.ts:312, :537, :556, then the plan at :372-379). A recompute on a tree where the adopt already landed therefore produces a plan that leaves out every file the adopt wrote, and it is most likely empty.
- A waiter in a third worktree, still on the pre-sync tree with the same hash, matches at :649/:640 and adopts. On an empty plan, applySyncWritePlan writes nothing and returns true (sync.ts:490). That waiter replays "0 files changed" while its own docs stay stale. This is exactly the harm SF1 named.
- The window is narrow:
  - Backlog backend only.
  - The adopt's sweep must fail transiently. If the recompute's own sweep also throws, runSync throws at :390 and capture writes no slot.
  - A concurrent waiter must exist in another worktree.
- Why it blocks anyway:
  - The new docstring at sync.ts:451-453 asserts "any later reuse is re-gated by the pre-image check, so it fails safe". That is false here: a subset or empty plan carries no pre-image for the files it omits.
  - This PR appears to have created the path. N3's throw-to-false guard came in b88fc820 (round 1 reviewed it as a fix). Before N3, a throwing adopt propagated and no slot was written. Please confirm with `git log -L` on adoptOrAbandon; I could not.
- Fix, either option a few lines, and both cost something only on abandon:
  - (a) After an adopt that was attempted and did not accept, call options.rehash() again (when one is supplied) before compute, and key :690 by that value.
  - (b) Write no slot on the abandon path.
  - Test: an adopt that writes a file and then throws, plus a rehash that returns a different value on its second call. Assert the slot key equals the second value, or that no slot exists. A mutant that keeps the pre-adopt key must go red.
- Round 1's N-d reasoning ("fails safe ... re-gated by the pre-image check") was mine to catch and I missed the empty-plan case. The N-d docstring inherits that error.

WHAT THE LEADER ASKED, CHECKED
- Write sites:
  - writeResult has exactly one call site, advisory-lock.ts:690. It is keyed by keyHash from :678, which is options.rehash() whenever a rehasher is supplied.
  - Both the first-try path and the post-wait path reach it. So do the found-but-adopt-refused/threw path and the nothing-found path.
  - The adopt-accepted path returns at :686 and writes no slot.
  - unlock() (:768-777) writes no slot.
  - The only remaining use of the entry hash is :649, the while-waiting replay read, which writes nothing.
  - The production rehasher is the same function as the entry hasher (advisory-run.ts:145-155, :166).
- Reuse is not silently disabled:
  - commandInputHash keys on the root RELATIVE to the toplevel (advisory-lock.ts:390, :418), not the absolute path. Two worktrees with identical trees hash equal.
  - The holder rehashes before its run writes, so it keys the pre-write tree, and a clean waiter's entry hash matches it.
  - Covered end to end through runLockedCommand, which always supplies the rehasher, with real git:
    - :505-513, another worktree, computes === 1.
    - :479-485, same worktree, sync.
    - :106-170, same root, check, replayed byte-for-byte.
    - :172-214, a changed tree is not reused (the negative control).
- SF1 test, test/advisory-lock.test.ts:1302-1320:
  - It acquires on the first try (waited === false at :1314), then asserts rehashes === 1 (:1317) and slot key "h2" (:1318-1320).
  - A rehash-only-after-a-wait mutant goes red on both. The old "rehashes === 0" assertion is gone; I found no remnant.
- B1: done, at test/lcli792-advisory-command.test.ts:326 with `expect(await applySyncWritePlan(other, plans[0] as SyncWritePlan)).toBe(true)`. A writes-but-returns-false mutant goes red there.
- N-a: done, test/advisory-lock.test.ts:1376-1396.
  - The owner is recorded into adoptSawOwner inside adopt and asserted after the call (:1395-1396). The pid assertion is gone.
  - It is now live in BOTH iterations, including accept=false.
  - Release-before-adopt goes red through not.toBe(holderOwner).
  - Adopt-without-lock goes red through toBeDefined: the read throws, the throw is swallowed, and the variable stays undefined.
- N-b: done. test.skipIf(win32 || uid 0) at :1404, so the skip is visible.
- N-d: the docstring is at sync.ts:449-453. Its first half is right; its "fails safe" claim is wrong, per B2.
- DEC-282:
  - (a14) Q1: adopt runs under the lock, with the heartbeat started at :679, before :685. The order inside it holds: equal → skip (sync.ts:477), pre-image → write, otherwise refuse before any write (:478).
  - (a14) Q3: adopt and abandon are silent. Only unlock() emits a line, once per kind via onceNotices (:758-765), and nothing goes to stdout.
  - (a16): isLockSnapshotStale returns false for a same-host live pid whatever its age (:912-919).
  - All three hold.

SHOULD-FIX
None beyond B2.

NITS
- advisory-lock.ts:678 calls options.rehash() after the lock is created but before startHeartbeat (:679) and outside the try/finally (:680/:693-696). A throwing rehasher would leave the lock behind with no release.
  - The real hasher cannot throw: realGitRunner catches (:266-273), fileDigest catches (:438-446), canonicalPath catches (~:330).
  - But the seam is public, and this round made the call run on every acquire. Move the keyHash computation inside the try.
- advisory-lock.ts:493-496: the JSDoc still calls the default "correct when the caller acquired immediately". :498-501 now contradicts that.
- advisory-run.ts:164-165: "A holder that waited behind `sync`" still frames the rehash as wait-only.
- test/advisory-lock.test.ts:1322-1342: the waited half asserts the rehash count but not the "h4" key. Optional: :1093-1114 already pins post-wait keying.
- N-c: left, as ruled.
- docs/: no lore page states the old "rehash only after a wait" rule. I grepped docs/ for rehash, "after a wait", "actual wait" and "waited behind".

COULD NOT CONFIRM WITHOUT A SHELL
- Any test or mutant result, including the writer's three mutants.
- B2 is not reproduced. I also have no data on how often a Backlog sweep fails transiently in practice.
- That N3's guard first landed in b88fc820 (ask for `git log -L '/function adoptOrAbandon/,+7:src/core/advisory-lock.ts'`).
- The changed-file set b88fc820..a42a863d, so DEC-182 (1) is unverified. Every file I read is in src/ or test/.
- Whether the windows-latest leg actually reports the skipIf test as skipped.

Verdict notes above, recorded verbatim: round 1 REQUEST CHANGES at b88fc820 (file sha256 a1f588b5f1f6d0adc3b9c04b2ce095070566573e8a2a8b9be1d9eeb086bbbd20, 7292 bytes) and round 2 REQUEST CHANGES at a42a863d (sha256 bd6d48363a855526e14103d5e93d7ff95bbe2eeac1e00310d930bd65b21c3984, 7478 bytes). Round 3 pushed at 2d6cf761 (no result slot after an abandoned adopt, rehash inside the try, stale wording); awaiting its review. adoptOrAbandon first landed in b88fc820 (git log -L). GATES LBUMP.
